$comment: academic-light palettes. Shape: palettes by name, each with a kind (categorical | sequential | diverging), colors with localized names, and role mappings. The categorical palette passes `checkPalette` (cli/palettes.js) on the theme background #ffffff: at least 3:1 contrast per color and CIEDE2000 >= 8 between every pair under simulated protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia. See README.md.

okabe-ito-dark.description: Okabe-Ito, darkened for at least 3:1 contrast on a white background and re-separated for color-vision deficiency. Black (the ink) and yellow (olive once darkened, and confused with orange) are left out. Ordered so the first two series are the most distinct.
okabe-ito-dark.source: Okabe, M. and Ito, K. (2008). Color Universal Design (CUD): how to make figures and presentations that are friendly to colorblind people. https://jfly.uni-koeln.de/color/ Darkened in OKLab (hue kept) by stepdeck.

viridis.description: Viridis, perceptually uniform and readable in grey and with color-vision deficiency. A fill scale: its light end is not meant for thin marks on white.
viridis.source: viridis, by Stéfan van der Walt and Nathaniel Smith (matplotlib), released under CC0.

blue-red.description: Blue to red through a light grey midpoint; the two arms stay distinct with color-vision deficiency. A fill scale: the midpoint is meant to sit near the background.
blue-red.source: ColorBrewer RdBu (5 classes), Cynthia Brewer, Mark Harrower and The Pennsylvania State University, Apache License 2.0.
